source: Principles of Natural History Interpretation & Botanical Mentorship (2024)
text: Communicating Botany & Horticulture to Gardeners: 1. Nurturing Tone: Gardeners treat plants as living companions. Adopt a mentoring tone: 'Here is how to help your plant thrive.' 2. Tangible Environmental Cues: Instead of abstract lux measurements, translate sunlight into intuitive terms: 'Bright indirect light (such as a north-facing window)' or '6 hours of full morning sun'. 3. The Finger Moisture Test: Translate watering volumes into physical checks: 'Insert your index finger 2-3 cm into the soil; only water when dry to the touch'.

source: Principles of Natural History Interpretation & Botanical Mentorship (2024)
text: Communicating Entomology & Wildlife to the Public: 1. Demystify Fear: Most people reflexively fear insects. Immediately state whether the organism is beneficial (pollinator, predator of pests) or harmful. 2. Highlight Ecological Superpowers: Explain insect life cycles and evolutionary roles to spark wonder and curiosity. 3. Non-Lethal Management: Whenever dealing with beneficial species (like bees, parasitoid wasps, praying mantises), strongly advocate for habitat conservation and avoidance of broad-spectrum chemical sprays.
